title: Programs
text: Alongside research and teaching I build and run externally funded international programs. These are operating enterprises with budgets, partners, donors and reporting obligations, not standing committees.

title: Programs
text:
Taiwan Research Academy
An intensive residential academic program bringing graduate students and faculty together to study Taiwan’s political system, economic development and public policy. The 2026 cycle ran eight days in June with eighteen students and sixteen faculty and guest speakers drawn from multiple institutions.
Institutional partners include the Taiwan Foundation for Democracy, Academia Sinica, National Chung Hsing University, National Taiwan University, and the George H. W. Bush Foundation for U.S.–China Relations.

title: Programs
text:
Taiwan Studies Initiative
The umbrella for Taiwan-focused research, curriculum and public engagement at UT Dallas, supported by a multi-year Taiwan Ministry of Education Taiwan Studies Program award.

title: Programs
text:
Mandarin and Culture Program
Delivered jointly with National Chung Hsing University under the Taiwan Ministry of Education’s Mandarin education framework, bringing language instruction and cultural programming to the North Texas region.

title: Programs
text:
Convening and public engagement
I have organized and spoken at Taiwan policy and research convenings hosted at UT Dallas, National Chung Hsing University, Academia Sinica, the University of St. Thomas, Sam Houston State University, and the Greater Dallas Taiwanese Chamber of Commerce, and have served as an invited speaker on China’s digital governance at the American Bar Association.

title: Research
text: My research uses data science methods to explain and prescribe social and political problems. For twenty-five years that has meant electoral behavior and democratization in East Asia, measured with whatever instrument political conditions allow — probability samples where they are possible, and generative methods where they are not.

title: Research
text:
Synthetic data and generative methods
My most active line. It brings together silicon sampling with large language models to generate synthetic survey respondents; Bayesian networks and directed acyclic graphs with do-calculus to identify media effects where experiments are impossible; Wasserstein GANs for modeling political support dynamics; and ROC-based out-of-sample validation as the discipline on all of it.
The problem I want to solve is validation. The field is producing synthetic respondents faster than it is agreeing how to distinguish a good one from a bad one. I am developing a four-part protocol — out-of-sample ROC, distributional distance on the joint rather than the marginals, subgroup recovery, and known-answer backtesting against historical elections — with an accompanying open R package.

title: Research
text:
Measurement when political space closes
As Co-Principal Investigator of the Hong Kong Election Study I helped run an annual probability survey from 2015 to 2023, spanning a period in which the territory moved from contested electoral politics to a substantially closed political system. The methodological claim running through this work is that standard attitudinal instruments — internal political efficacy above all — do not carry fixed meaning across regime types.

title: Research
text:
Media effects and generational cleavage
Taiwan is an unusually clean setting for studying partisan media effects, because channel partisanship is explicit and recognized by viewers. My work incorporates television viewership directly as a predictor of party support across the KMT, DPP and TPP, and examines generational structure in those effects.

title: Research
text:
AI readiness in governance
Applied work on AI readiness in public governance and digital democracy in Taiwan, and on generative methods for integrating public preferences into carbon management and energy policy.

title: Teaching
text:
Course materials
The graduate sequence is authored in Quarto, which produces a book and the lecture slides from one source, so notes and slides cannot drift apart and the corpus can be regenerated when a package API changes. Materials are published openly and version-controlled.
I have built and delivered R, Quarto and Shiny workshop curricula, and a Quarto + Git + GitHub Pages workshop with slides, templates and an instructor guide so other instructors can run it without me. A full list is on the workshops page.

title: Teaching
text:
Mentored research
Students who want to coauthor with me are encouraged to prepare CV, portfolio and proposal materials before scheduling a meeting. Recent conference papers written with graduate students cover generational cleavages in media effects, Bayesian network models of media influence, comparative democratic decline using NLP, the political economy of housing capital in China, structural topic models of American foreign policy opinion, partisan network analysis, and time-series machine learning on US–China trade. Regions of studies include Taiwan, Hong Kong, China and US.

title: Workshops
text:
Hands-on teaching outside the classroom — multi-day and multi-week workshops for graduate students, faculty and the general public, delivered in the United States and Taiwan since 2019.
These are working sessions rather than lectures. Participants arrive with a laptop and leave with something that runs: a rendered document, a published site, a model they fitted themselves. Most have no prior programming background, which is a design constraint rather than an obstacle.

title: Workshops
text:
Curricula I have built
The sessions above are deliveries of material I designed. Each curriculum is authored in Quarto, version-controlled, and published openly so that other instructors can run it without me — which is the point. A workshop that only its author can teach is a talk with exercises.


R, Quarto and Shiny for interactive data analysis


Multi-session · graduate and faculty audiences


A sequence built around a single public dataset, carrying learners from import and cleaning through visual exploration to a deployed interactive application. Using one dataset throughout means participants are never relearning a domain while also learning a tool.


RQuartoShinyDeployment




Quarto, Git and GitHub Pages


One day · researchers at any career stage


Slides, project templates, reference material and an instructor guide for building and publishing a reproducible academic website. Participants finish with a live site under their own domain or a GitHub Pages address.


QuartoGitPublishingInstructor guide




Math and Coding Camp


Pre-semester bridge program · incoming graduate students


The bridge that makes a graduate methods sequence accessible to students arriving without a quantitative background. Linear algebra and probability refreshers alongside a working R environment, so that week one of the first methods course is not also week one of programming.

title: Workshops
text:
How I run them

Three commitments carry across every workshop I teach: everything is reproducible from source, so participants can rebuild what they made after they go home; everyone publishes, because work that only exists on one laptop tends not to survive the week; and the data is real, with the missingness and ambiguity intact, because cleaned teaching datasets teach the wrong lesson about what analysis actually involves.

Workshop material and course repositories are on GitHub. For graduate courses taught within a degree programme, see teaching; for conference papers and invited lectures, see talks.

title: About
text:
Teaching Social Data Analytics and Research core curriculum: Methods of Data Collection and Production, Data Visualization, Information Management, and Knowledge Mining.
Since 2023 I have directed the university’s Taiwan Studies Initiative and Taiwan Research Academy, which together carry external support from the Taiwan Ministry of Education, the Taiwan Foundation for Democracy, and private donors. I also built a dual degree program in data science with National Chung Hsing University, signed in 2023 and first enrolling students in 2024.
My research uses synthetic data methods to study electoral behavior in East Asia and the United States, with recent work on media effects in Taiwan elections, synthetic data, and the limits of language models.

title: Requesting a recommendation letter
text: If you would like me to write you a recommendation letter, please read the advice of Gary King of Harvard University, which remains the clearest account I know of what makes a letter worth reading, together with what I need from you.

title: Requesting a recommendation letter
text:
What to send me
Email the following to kyho@utdallas.edu:

An updated CV
If you have taken my courses, the title of your project and your final grade
Two to three paragraphs on the highlights of your experience and academic achievements
The full address and addressee for up to three recipients of the letter

As much lead time as you can give me is appreciated.

title: Requesting a recommendation letter
text:
Dr. King’s advice

Letters of Recommendation
If you need a letter of recommendation from a faculty member, and we’ve worked closely together in some capacity beyond class (e.g., RA, TF, co-author, dissertation advisee, etc.), I’m happy to help out. However, if you have worked more closely with some other faculty member, a letter from that person is much more likely to be useful to you. Wherever you are applying will not merely want to know that someone endorses your candidacy (every letter does that!); the crucial component is that the person writing the letter knows you well, through a diverse array of experiences.
If you think that person is me, then please send me, along with your request, one email to king@harvard.edu with the following as separate (nonzipped) attachments in PDF format (not Word and no paper please): copies of whatever documents you plan to submit to the organization to which you are applying that you think will be useful; a curriculum vitae; transcripts; test scores, etc.; and a confidential “sliced bread” memo (i.e., why I am better than…) addressed to me. This memo should not be a draft letter of recommendation, but instead should include a list of bullet points you want to make sure I remember when I start writing. These items can include how I got to know you and standard cv items (prizes won, etc.), but should also include relevant anecdotes that might make useful stories to illustrate characteristics of you or your work (e.g., solved a problem in five minutes that King had been working on full time for six weeks). This is not the time for modesty (only you and I will ever see it), and don’t assume I will remember something if you exclude it. Include a very short (2-3 sentence) abstract or main finding of your thesis or other current work. If your record includes something negative (such as if you were in graduate school for too long), include your plausible explanation for what happened, if there is one.
I’ll send all letters directly to the organization to which you’re applying if you include an editable list of names and addresses, or to the Harvard dossier service, which sends them out for us. Please use king-assist@iq.harvard.edu instead of my email if the organization to which you are applying uses a web interface that will send me emails.
As much lead time as you can provide would be appreciated.

Source: Letters of Recommendation, Gary King, Harvard University.
Before you write to me, consider the first paragraph carefully. A letter from the person who knows your work best is worth more than a letter from the most senior person willing to sign one.
